title: 2005 HMMT February Team Round 2 Problem 1
statement: Let \(0<m \leq n\) be integers. How many different (i.e., noncongruent) dominoes can be formed by choosing two squares of an \(m \times n\) array?

solutions.text:
We must have \(0 \leq a<m, 0 \leq b<n, a \leq b\), and \(a\) and \(b\) not both 0 . The number of pairs \((a, b)\) with \(b<a<m\) is \(m(m-1) / 2\), so the answer is

\[m n-\frac{m(m-1)}{2}-1=m n-\frac{m^{2}-m+2}{2} .\]
